your_book:
Friday was a split-session story for Jaleel's book. The two biggest winners drove most of the noise: Adobe surged +6.1% to $3,526.71 — the largest single-day dollar move in the portfolio — and ServiceNow ripped +7.44% to $2,271.94, likely on earnings-adjacent momentum in enterprise software. Together those two positions added meaningful paper recovery against the book's standing -$792.42 unrealized loss. Abbott chipped in a clean +2.29% and sits as the book's best open position at +19.2%. The constructive side of Friday is real, but it doesn't paper over the structural drag: nine of eighteen holdings are still underwater on a cost basis, and the overall book remains -3.64% in the red.

The clearest divergence sits in RKLB, which fell another -8.69% Friday and now sits -30.1% from cost at $1,789.48. The system rates it AVOID with a QARP of 46.4 — the only holding carrying that label — yet it remains an 8.5% weight. That's a thesis-versus-price gap that is widening, not narrowing. LULU (+3.3% Friday) is a subtler version of the same problem: a nice bounce to $1,028.52, but the FY guidance cut, Americas comps down five straight quarters, and tariff margin pressure haven't gone away. A green day doesn't fix a broken trend. BSX also ticked up +1.54%, but its FY26 growth guidance was slashed and management guides flat through Q3 — next catalyst is Tuesday, July 29.

What to watch into next week: BSX earnings Tuesday will test whether the guidance cut was kitchen-sinking or genuine deterioration. UBER dropped -4.31% Friday to $1,055.04 and is -7.9% from cost — the STRONG BUY rating and 78.9 QARP suggest the thesis is intact, but back-to-back pressure warrants monitoring the narrative. ADBE's +6.1% is welcome but the risk flag is clear: the market is trading fear of AI disruption, not the numbers, so gains here can evaporate fast. The book has essentially zero cash ($ 0.38), so any rebalancing or tax-loss action requires selling something first.
